notes.japanese: 貧道は、あなたの病を癒しに来たのです。
notes.problem: The monk's only self-word 貧道 is flattened to plain I, losing the clerical colour that lets him claim authority while staying unexplained.
notes.span: I have come to cure your disease.
notes.suggestion: "This poor monk has come to cure your disease."
notes.sureness: Fairly sure; the bible flags 貧道 as marked, and a period dictionary or house decision on clerical self-reference would settle it.

notes.japanese: 勿体らしくしやがんでゐる。
notes.problem: Portentously makes the monk ominous, where 勿体らしく is merely self-important and the crux requires him to stay neither sage nor sinister.
notes.span: squats there portentously, in the attitude of a turkey.
notes.suggestion: "squats there with an air of importance, in the attitude of a turkey."
notes.sureness: Quite sure on the dictionary sense of 勿体らしい as pompous; period usage would confirm the exact nuance.

notes.japanese: 瓶の口からは、芬々たる酒香が、間断なく、劉の鼻を襲つて来る。
notes.problem: Heavy impoverishes 芬々たる, which is richly fragrant and pleasant, and that pleasantness is part of the thirst-torture.
notes.span: From the mouth of the jar the heavy smell of wine comes without break to assail his nose.
notes.suggestion: "From the mouth of the jar the rich fragrant smell of wine comes without break to assail his nose."
notes.sureness: Moderately sure; I know 芬々 as sweet fragrance, and checking the house's agreed rendering of 酒香 elsewhere would settle whether heavy breaks the network.

notes.japanese: 酒を入れた素焼の瓶を一つ、劉の枕もとへ持つて来させた。
notes.problem: Filled with wine expands 酒を入れた, stating fullness the text does not state and anticipating the brimming wine imagined later in p46.
notes.span: he had an unglazed earthen jar filled with wine brought to Liu's pillow.
notes.suggestion: "he had an unglazed earthen jar with wine in it brought to Liu's pillow."
notes.sureness: Quite sure on the literal difference between入れた and filled; minor, but a check of jar-wording consistency would settle it.

notes.japanese: 昔日の劉の健康なり家産なりが、失はれたのも、至極、当然な話であらう。
notes.problem: The doublet expands a single closing formula and makes the third answer weightier, where the three answers must stay parallel and evenly weighted.
notes.span: is entirely natural, and a matter of course.
notes.suggestion: "that the health and estate of the Liu of former days should have been lost would be only natural."
notes.sureness: Fairly sure as a matter of enumeration; the desk's ear on the three closings together would settle it.

data.say: Apart from these small losses the part keeps tableau, sensation and the undecided close faithfully.
